Start a course folder for the instructor toolkit

Source: R/toolkit-course.R
new_course.Rd

The instructor toolkit keeps a course's teaching materials in one folder that you can edit, extend and re-run with your own data. new_course() creates the folder:

Usage

new_course(path, title = NULL, instructor = NULL, overwrite = FALSE)

course_materials(course = ".")

Arguments

path

the folder to create. It may exist already, but must not already hold a course.json unless overwrite = TRUE.

title

course title. Defaults to the folder name.

instructor

instructor name(s), optional.

overwrite

replace an existing course.json and README.md.

course

the course folder.

Value

new_course() returns the course path, invisibly. course_materials() returns a tibble with one row per material: name, type ("lab" or "chapter"), title, path, source ("toolkit" for labs built with new_lab(), "built-in" for copies of the package's labs, "book" for chapters copied from the mirtverse book, "own" otherwise) and data (the data a toolkit lab uses).

Details

  • course.json: the course title and instructor.

  • README.md: a short how-to for whoever opens the folder next.

  • labs/: interactive labs (learnr tutorials), one folder each, made with new_lab() or copy_lab().

  • chapters/: notes chapters (R Markdown), made with new_chapter() or copy_chapter().

  • data/: your raw data files, for reference.

course_materials() lists the labs and chapters in a course folder. It scans labs/ and chapters/, so materials you add by hand are listed too.

All toolkit functions take paths, never ask questions, and return the path they wrote (invisibly) or a tibble, so they can be scripted.

See also

new_lab(), copy_lab(), copy_chapter(), check_material()

Examples

course <- file.path(tempdir(), "irt-course")
new_course(course, title = "EDPY 507: Item response theory")
copy_lab("model-choice", course)
course_materials(course)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   name         type  title                                    path  source data 
#>   <chr>        <chr> <chr>                                    <chr> <chr>  <chr>
#> 1 model-choice lab   Lab 1: Choosing a model the board can d… /tmp… built… NA
